page.title: Docs Site Decisions
page.lede: Three invented decisions about a documentation site, to show the format. Read top down: [[41]] sets the direction for the rest.

layers: One card sets where the docs build lives; the cards below are answerable whatever you pick here.
How the move is carried out. Each card says which answer above it depends on.
follow: When should it come back? Blank means the next report.
Anything in particular to show in more detail?
What should I look into first?

impact.effect: publishing no longer depends on one laptop
impact.wait: the local build stays; [[42]] and [[43]] wait
impact.reach: every docs contributor, and anyone who publishes by hand
impact.undo: switch the pipeline off; one config change

tldr: The docs build runs on a laptop today
Move it to CI, or keep it local
cards.context: You last saw the build fail twice on a stale cache ([[38]]) · now you pick where it runs.
cards.what: Where the documentation site is built and published from: a maintainer's laptop, as today, or the CI pipeline.
cards.why: Two broken publishes this month came from a local cache. Blocks [[42]] and [[43]].
cards.whyask: Moving the build changes who can publish; the team may rely on publishing by hand.
cards.ifunanswered: I leave the build on the laptop and carry on with other work.
o: Keep building on a laptop. Nothing changes; the maintainer publishes by hand.
Stale-cache failures continue at about two a month.
Build and publish from CI on every merge to main, with the local build kept for previews.
Publishing no longer depends on one machine; about 4 minutes of CI per merge.
The local build stays until you answer; [[42]] and [[43]] wait.

a.happens: Nothing changes; the maintainer publishes by hand.
a.cost: About two failed publishes a month.

b.happens: Every merge to main builds and publishes the site from CI.
b.undo: Switch the pipeline off; one config change.
b.cost: About 4 minutes of CI per merge.

cards.reason: both failures were read in the build logs
cards.unknown: whether anyone publishes from a fork
cards.evidence: Build logs for both failed publishes show the same stale cache directory.

impact.effect: old links keep working through twelve redirects
impact.wait: the first CI publish waits for this answer
impact.reach: external readers and every site linking to the old pages
impact.undo: (a) remove the redirect lines; (b) none — once search engines drop the old URLs, redirects added later do not win the ranking back

tldr: The CI build changes some page URLs
Redirect them, or let them break
cards.context: Only matters if [[41]] is (b) · you pick how old links behave.
cards.what: What happens to the twelve page URLs that change shape when the site is built in CI.
cards.why: Needed before the first CI publish. Blocks nothing else.
cards.whyask: Breaking public links is a call about readers, not about the build.
o: Add a redirect for each of the twelve URLs.
Old links keep working; twelve lines of redirect config to maintain.
Let the old URLs return not found.
External links break; search ranking for those pages is lost and cannot be won back on demand.
The first CI publish waits for this answer.

a.happens: Twelve redirects are added to the site config before the first CI publish.
a.undo: Remove the redirect lines; nothing else changes.
a.who: Readers following old links, who land on the new pages.
a.cost: Twelve lines of redirect config to keep.

b.happens: The twelve old URLs return not found from the first CI publish.
b.undo: Cannot be fully undone: once search engines drop the old URLs, redirects added later do not win the ranking back.
b.who: External readers and every site linking to the old pages.

cards.reason: the URL list is observed; the traffic to them is estimated
cards.unknown: how many external sites link to the old URLs

impact.effect: (a) no visual change; (b) the site matches the logo
impact.wait: the site keeps the blue meanwhile

tldr: The CI build can apply a new theme
Pick a colour, or keep the current one
cards.what: Which accent colour the rebuilt site uses.
cards.why: Nothing forces it; raised because the move touches the theme files anyway.
cards.whyask: A taste call; no fact settles it.
o: Switch to the green from the logo.
The site matches the logo; screenshots in the guides look dated until refreshed.
The site keeps the blue meanwhile.
